newsitem.title: ESTONIA: HANSA SAYS EYES AGRICULTURAL BANK SERIOUSLY.
newsitem.headline: HANSA SAYS EYES AGRICULTURAL BANK SERIOUSLY.

text.p: Hansabank, Estonia's leading bank, said on Wednesday that it is seriously mulling the idea of buying into Lithuania's state-run Agricultural Bank.

"We are seriously considering participating in the privatisation of the Agricultural Bank," Rain Lohmus, Hansabank's vice chairman, told Reuters, confirming a report in Wednesday's edition of Aripaev.
He added that the bank could take other routes into Lithuania's banking market, which seems to have recovered from a crisis which erupted in late 1995 with the closure of two of its top banks.
"There are other options (to enter Lithuania)," he said, adding that the establishment of a branch is also possible.
"The situation is different in Latvia, where the sale of Deutsche Lettische Bank was being pushed...Lithuania has not said that it wants to sell the Agricultural Bank today," Lohmus said.
Hansabank last June acquired Latvian Deutsche Lettische Bank, which it has renamed Hansabank Latvija. It was the first cross-border acquisition by a Baltic bank.
Vaclovas Litvinas, the chairman of the Agricultural Bank, told Reuters that the bank was in talks with Hansabank and that the Estonian bank was examining its financial situation.
The Agricultural Bank is one of two state-run banks in Lithuania which have been slated for privatisation as part of the government's plan to reform the sector.
